observation_summary: The code throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException because it attempts to access a character at an index equal to the string length during a search for a wrap position.
hypothesis: The while loop condition in findWrapPos incorrectly uses '<=' when checking the string length, allowing the index to reach text.length(), which is an invalid index for charAt(). Furthermore, the logic attempting to search for whitespace beyond the specified width is flawed and unnecessary for the intended behavior of cutting the string.
prediction: Removing the while loop that incorrectly scans beyond the string length will prevent the index out of bounds exception and correctly return the calculated wrap position.
experiment_rationale: The fix removes the problematic while loop entirely, which was the source of the out-of-bounds access. This confirms that the loop was not only causing the exception but was also logically incorrect for the intended string wrapping behavior.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic boundary condition error where a loop condition allowed an index to exceed the valid range of a string. The fix involves removing the incorrect loop logic that was performing an invalid check, which is a quintessential 'Checking' defect (incorrect predicate logic/boundary validation).
evidence_used: The stack trace shows a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 937.
The buggy code at line 937 uses 'pos <= text.length()' in a while loop condition.
The fix removes the entire while loop that was performing the invalid index access.
The bug report explicitly mentions that the first expression in the while loop condition should use a '<' instead of '<='.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the loop is part of an algorithm, the root cause is specifically the incorrect boundary check (predicate) that leads to an exception, which is more precisely classified as Checking.
